chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Folk, blues and religious music; Rosetta Tharpe and Ethel Waters
summary: He likes folk if not abused, Lonnie Johnson blues, Rosetta Tharpe and Ethel Waters.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: What about - I guess it will be my final thing - what about other forms of music, like for instance could you tell me what was happening like gospel and spiritual music... and what was the folk music like?
I like some folk music if you don't abuse it, but I don't know how to explain it. If you don't abuse it, it's beautiful music, if you don't abuse it.
Did you listen to any old blues - do you remember any in particular?
I listen to a whole lot of this noise I hear around here.
I'm talking about in the 30's and 20's and stuff like that.
Blues? You know, like Lonnie Johnson, guys like that.
Yes, somebody knew how to play the blues.
My final thing will be, what about the field of religious music, who were some great religious singers that you know?
I can't think of the name and I played for him. I made a whole lot of records for him too.
Who was the agent for black religious music, gospel and spiritual and stuff like that?

I know who you're talking about. The last time I saw him was down to the Central Plaza. I tell you one you might - maybe you won't like him but I really did - I don't know if you know Rosetta Thorpe. I don't care what Ethel Waters sings, I love it.
Oh, you mean Ethel Waters had something against Rosetta Thorpe?
No, you asked me one question and I'm answering another one. I finished with Thorpe and now I'm on Ethel.
